classification.difficultyReason: Use the three explicitly indicated triangle pairs to derive ratios, then connect the diagonal partition to equal intercepted lengths and the midpoint conclusion.

content.prompt:
Let $ABCD$ be a trapezium with $AB\parallel CD$. Let the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meet at $O$.

Let the line through $O$ parallel to $AB$ meet $AD$ at $P$ and $BC$ at $Q$.

By considering the pairs of triangles $ADB$ and $POD$, $BDC$ and $QOB$, and $AOB$ and $COD$, prove that $O$ is the midpoint of $PQ$.

answer.short:
$OP=OQ$, so $O$ is the midpoint of $PQ$.

The three indicated triangle similarities give $OP=OQ=\dfrac{AB\times CD}{AB+CD}$.
answer.worked:
Since $PO\parallel AB$, $\angle DPO=\angle DAB$ (corresponding angles) and $\angle PDO=\angle ADB$ (common angle at $D$). Thus $\triangle ADB\sim\triangle PDO$ (AAA), giving
$$\frac{OP}{AB}=\frac{DO}{DB}.$$
Since $OQ\parallel DC$, $\angle BOQ=\angle BDC$ (corresponding angles) and $\angle OBQ=\angle DBC$ (common angle at $B$). Thus $\triangle BDC\sim\triangle BOQ$ (AAA), giving
$$\frac{OQ}{CD}=\frac{BO}{BD}.$$
Also $\angle AOB=\angle COD$ (vertically opposite angles) and $\angle ABO=\angle CDO$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$). Thus $\triangle AOB\sim\triangle COD$ (AAA), so
$$\frac{BO}{DO}=\frac{AB}{CD}.$$
Let $AB=a$ and $CD=b$. Since $BD=BO+DO$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{BO}{DO}&=\frac{a}{b}\\\frac{BD}{DO}&=\frac{a+b}{b}\\\frac{DO}{BD}&=\frac{b}{a+b}\\\frac{BO}{BD}&=\frac{a}{a+b}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore
$$\begin{align*}OP&=a\times\frac{b}{a+b}\\OP&=\frac{ab}{a+b}\\OQ&=b\times\frac{a}{a+b}\\OQ&=\frac{ab}{a+b}.\end{align*}$$
Hence $OP=OQ$. As $P,O,Q$ are collinear with $O$ between $P$ and $Q$, $O$ is the midpoint of $PQ$.
